rule.title: Diamond Sleet APT Scheduled Task Creation
rule.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: Se creó en un servidor Windows una tarea programada llamada "\Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" cuyo contenido incluye la cadena "uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ". Ambos indicadores coinciden con lo que se observó de Diamond Sleet al explotar la vulnerabilidad CVE-2023-42793 de TeamCity.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 4698 (tarea programada creada) del log Security cuyo TaskName es exactamente "\Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" y cuyo TaskContent (el XML de la tarea) contiene "uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ". Para que el evento exista, debe estar habilitada la auditoría Audit Other Object Access Events.
es.why_it_matters: Según la referencia de Microsoft, Diamond Sleet usó esta tarea para persistir y ejecutar código después de comprometer servidores TeamCity mediante CVE-2023-42793 (MITRE ATT&CK T1053.005, Scheduled Task). Como un servidor de CI/CD comprometido expone código fuente, secretos y pipelines, existe riesgo para la cadena de suministro.
triage_steps: Identifique el host (Computer) y confirme si tiene TeamCity instalado o expuesto. Revise la versión para saber si es vulnerable a CVE-2023-42793.
Analice TaskContent. Extraiga Command, Arguments, el usuario de ejecución (Principal) y los triggers, y anote cualquier binario o ruta referenciada.
Revise SubjectUserName y SubjectDomainName para saber qué cuenta creó la tarea. Normalmente es la cuenta de servicio de TeamCity o SYSTEM.
Obtenga el hash del binario referenciado en la tarea y búsquelo en EDR y en inteligencia de amenazas. No lo ejecute.
En el mismo host, revise los eventos de +/- 15 minutos: procesos hijos del servicio TeamCity (java.exe), PowerShell, descargas, nuevos servicios y eventos 4688/4697/4720.
En los logs web de TeamCity, busque solicitudes a la API de tokens o de usuarios provenientes de IP externas antes de que se creara la tarea.
Busque el mismo TaskName, la misma cadena o el mismo hash en otros endpoints, y revise alertas previas del host.
false_positives: El campo falsepositives de la regla dice Unknown. La combinación de nombre de tarea y cadena es muy específica, así que no se esperan causas legítimas.
Ejercicios de red team o emulación de amenazas que reproducen este IOC de forma intencional. Confírmelo con el equipo responsable.
response_steps: Si se confirma el IOC, aísle el host de la red con el EDR. Conserve antes la memoria, el XML de la tarea y el binario referenciado.
Deshabilite la tarea (no la elimine hasta haber recolectado evidencia) y bloquee el hash y las conexiones salientes asociadas.
Aplique el parche de TeamCity para CVE-2023-42793. Revoque los tokens de API y cuentas creados y rote los secretos almacenados en el servidor CI/CD.
Revise la integridad de los builds y artefactos generados desde el compromiso. Luego reconstruya el servidor desde una imagen limpia y escale a respuesta a incidentes.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel critical se justifica porque es un IOC exacto de una campaña APT conocida en un servidor CI/CD, con muy baja probabilidad de falso positivo.

en.summary: A Windows host created a scheduled task named "\Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" whose content includes the string "uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ". Both indicators match what was observed from Diamond Sleet when it exploited TeamCity CVE-2023-42793.
en.what_it_detects: Security event 4698 (scheduled task created) where TaskName is exactly "\Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" and the TaskContent XML contains "uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ". The event is only logged if Audit Other Object Access Events is enabled.
en.why_it_matters: According to the Microsoft reference, Diamond Sleet used this task to persist and run code after compromising TeamCity servers through CVE-2023-42793 (MITRE ATT&CK T1053.005, Scheduled Task). A compromised CI/CD server exposes source code, secrets and pipelines, which puts the supply chain at risk.
triage_steps: Identify the host (Computer) and check whether it runs or exposes TeamCity. Check the version to see if it is vulnerable to CVE-2023-42793.
Parse TaskContent. Extract Command, Arguments, the run-as Principal and the triggers, and note any referenced binary or path.
Check SubjectUserName and SubjectDomainName to see which account created the task. Usually this is the TeamCity service account or SYSTEM.
Get the hash of the binary referenced by the task and look it up in EDR and threat intelligence. Do not run it.
On the same host, review events within +/- 15 minutes: child processes of the TeamCity service (java.exe), PowerShell, downloads, new services and 4688/4697/4720 events.
In the TeamCity web logs, look for requests to the token or user API from external IPs before the task was created.
Search other endpoints for the same TaskName, string or hash, and review earlier alerts for the host.
false_positives: The rule's falsepositives field says Unknown. The task name and string together are highly specific, so no legitimate cause is expected.
Red team or threat-emulation exercises that deliberately replay this IOC. Confirm with the team that runs them.
response_steps: If the IOC is confirmed, isolate the host with EDR. First preserve memory, the task XML and the referenced binary.
Disable the task (do not delete it until evidence is collected), then block the hash and the related outbound connections.
Apply the TeamCity patch for CVE-2023-42793. Revoke API tokens and accounts that were created, and rotate secrets stored on the CI/CD server.
Check the integrity of builds and artifacts produced since the compromise. Then rebuild the server from a clean image and escalate to incident response.
en.severity_rationale: Critical fits because this is an exact IOC from a known APT campaign on a CI/CD server, with very low false-positive likelihood.

positive.description: Event 4698 on a TeamCity build server: the exact Diamond Sleet task name, and task XML that contains the campaign string in its arguments.

negative.description: A legitimate scheduled task created on the same TeamCity server with a different name and content that does not contain the campaign string.
Same task name, but TaskContent does not contain the campaign string, so the contains condition fails.
